title: Scientists Just Found a New Wild Cat. It's Smaller Than a House Cat

scenes.text: Scientists just found a new species of wild cat. The first in 100 years.
It's called the tilcayo. About four pounds. Smaller than most house cats.
It lives in Bolivia's cloud forests, where the Andes drop into the Amazon.
Everyone assumed it was a tiger cat. Then a sanctuary biologist looked closer. The DNA matched nothing.
The last new living cat species was named in 1923. This one was hiding in plain sight.
A whole species of cat, and we only named it in 2026. What else is out there?

description:
In September 2026, scientists described the tilcayo, Leopardus tilcayo, a new species of wild cat from the Yungas cloud forests of Bolivia, the first new living cat species named in more than 100 years.
It weighs about 2 kilograms, around 4 pounds, smaller than most house cats, with light brown fur and large rosettes. It had been mistaken for a northern tiger cat until genetic tests, published in Current Biology, showed it was a distinct species. The last new cat was the pampas cat in 1923.
Do you think there are more unknown mammals hiding in the rainforest?
thumbnail_text: NEW WILD CAT. FIRST IN 100 YEARS
first_comment: Scat samples suggest the tilcayo eats small rodents and camera footage hints it hunts at night. If you could name a new species, what would you call it?
